source_title: Quote of the day by Ian McKellen
source_excerpt: From leading a life in wartime in Northern England to the peak of global cinema, Ian McKellen has surely come a long way in his journey. Long before he became a household name as Magneto and Gandalf, he was widely regarded as the undisputed titan of the British stage. His rise to global blockbuster fame in his sixties stands as one of the most remarkable second acts in film history. Todayâs quote from the veteran star is about understanding that rather than living and doing things for external validation or for social relief, there are times when you simply need to look out for yourself and do things just because.The quote from Ian McKellen reads, âI think validation will come if your work is good." And so it's better to concentrate on how I get good work. And for me, good work is probably to do a job I haven't done before. I'm always looking for something different. And to work with people who are going to encourage you and support you and get the best out of you.âWhat does the quote mean?Ian McKellen said this quote in an interview that he gave during the promotional campaign for his film âThe Good Liar; (2019), where he starred alongside Dame Helen Mirren. In the interview, he discussed his career choices, seeking out supportive collaborators, and focusing on craft over external praise. The interview is from his chat with BAFTA (the British Academy of Film and Television Arts) for their âGuru / BAFTA Masterclass series.âIan McKellen's words are about shifting the focus in your life and in your goals from external approval to your own craft. The actor addresses a common pitfall in creative and professional life: chasing validation rather than personal growth and quality. In his quote, he also emphasizes the importance of continuous self-invention and stepping outside one's comfort zone.Taking his own example, he shared that for him, "good work" is inherently tied to novelty, aka taking on roles, challenges, or responsibilities he has never attempted before. Remaining in familiar territory may feel safe and earn easy praise, but real growth happens when you risk failure, step out of your comfort zone, and start trying something new that scares you and seems uncomfortable. Expanding your boundaries prevents stillness in life; it keeps you moving, it keeps your craft dynamic, and it naturally elevates the quality of what you produce.Other than that, the quoteâs meaning goes far beyond the limitations of your craft. Strip away the theater lighting and movie sets that he is talking about in the interview, and his philosophy becomes a more practical way for navigating daily life, personal relationships, and professional careers. Most of the time, we lead lives according to social beliefs, on the basis of what other people may say, monitoring social media likes, seeking constant reassurance, or tailoring choices to meet other peopleâs needs. However, the veteran actorâs words are all about developing an understanding within yourself that you are enough. May it be your craft, or may it be something from your everyday life; as long as you do good and lead with example rather than following others around, only then will you be able to truly succeed and move forward towards whatever you wish for.About Sir Ian McKellen, his early life and Hollywood fameSir Ian McKellen was born on May 25, 1939, in Burnley, Lancashire, England, and grew up in Wigan and Bolton. His childhood was deeply influenced by World War II, having spent his early years living through wartime Britain. From an early age, family trips to local theatrical productions and Shakespeare festivals at Stratford-upon-Avon helped hone his love for acting and theater.As for his studies, he earned a scholarship to St. Catharineâs College, Cambridge, to study English literature. During his time there, he fully immersed himself in acting and appeared in more than 20 student productions alongside contemporaries like Derek Jacobi and Trevor Nunn, to name a few. After graduating in 1961, he made his professional stage debut at the Belgrade Theatre in Coventry in âA Man for All Seasons.âAround the 90s, he started working in films and TV shows. In 1995, he co-wrote and starred in a modern cinematic adaptation of âRichard III,' which established his mark in the industry and helped him gain widespread acclaim.
